papers.title: Shank3 mutation disrupts the molecular signature of sleepiness across development.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used RNA-sequencing and polysomnography in Shank3 ΔC mice to examine how an autism-associated mutation alters the molecular response to sleepiness across development. The mutation blocked age-typical upregulation of neuronal growth and DNA repair pathways, while mutants persistently upregulated oxidative stress and protein synthesis pathways, impairing molecular responses to sleepiness.

papers.title: Sleep spindles stabilize human thalamocortical networks, inhibiting pathological disruptions
papers.summary: Using multi-night intracranial recordings across thalamic and cortical regions in 55 epilepsy patients, the study found bidirectional interactions between sleep spindles and interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs): spindles suppressed IEDs, while IEDs increased subsequent spindle probability. Nights with fewer IEDs had more frequent, longer, and faster spindles, suggesting spindles stabilize thalamocortical networks against pathological disruptions.

papers.title: Banxia Shumi Decoction Alleviates PCPA-Induced Insomnia and Regulates ADAM10 Expression via Melatonin Signaling in Rats.
papers.summary: Using a PCPA-induced rat insomnia model, this study showed that Banxia Shumi Decoction shortened sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration, with effects mediated via melatonin MT1/MT2 receptors. The decoction modulated sleep-related molecules CLOCK, PER1, CaMKII, GABARAP, mGluR1, and ADAM10, and these effects were reversed by the melatonin receptor antagonist luzindole.

papers.title: Sleep fragmentation drives local, network-specific epileptic activity in human epilepsy
papers.summary: Combined stereo-EEG and polysomnography in epilepsy patients showed that experimentally induced sleep arousals triggered rapid increases in interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) specifically in neocortical regions during N2 and N3 sleep, with larger effects in N2, but did not alter IED spatial propagation. These findings establish a causal role for sleep instability in locally driving pathological activity without recruiting broader epileptic networks.

papers.title: The Circadian Clock Component NPAS2 is modulated by AMPK and Regulates Substrate Utilization and Mitochondrial Function in Human Skeletal Muscle Cells.
authors: Dimitrius Santiago P S F Guimarães
papers.summary: In primary human myotubes, AMPKα silencing altered clock gene expression, reducing NPAS2 and DBP, and NPAS2 knockdown decreased basal oxidative metabolism, electron transport chain subunits, and increased β-oxidation flux. The findings identify NPAS2 as a downstream mediator linking AMPK-dependent circadian signaling to substrate utilization and mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm in platelet: an emerging therapeutic target in human diseases.
papers.summary: This review describes circadian oscillations in platelet function, including morning peaks in surface markers and afternoon peaks in aggregation, driven by the core clock and Rev-erbα signaling. It highlights platelets as emerging therapeutic targets in cardiovascular, neurological, and metabolic diseases and discusses circadian-targeting drugs.

papers.title: Glial Dysfunction and Memory Impairments in a Model of Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: Using single-nucleus RNA-sequencing of the hippocampus in a mouse model of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea, this study identified widespread transcriptomic perturbations in glia and neural stem cells. It validated reduced expression of QDPR, SOX8, LRRK2, NDUFS4, TFE3, and GLUT1, and confirmed impaired myelination, aberrant glial morphology, and diminished neural stem cells, linking glial dysfunction to memory impairments.

papers.title: Mirtazapine and Slow-Wave Sleep: A Focused Narrative Review of Human Polysomnographic Evidence.
papers.summary: This narrative review examined the neurobiological mechanisms and human polysomnographic evidence regarding mirtazapine's effects on sleep architecture, particularly N3 and slow-wave sleep. It found that while mirtazapine can produce measurable changes in objective sleep architecture, findings specifically for slow-wave sleep enhancement remain preliminary and mixed, with no consistent dose-response relationship established.

papers.title: Exploiting frontotemporal asymmetry in low-channel EEG emotion recognition via spectral fusion network.
papers.summary: The study introduced STSANet, a dual-branch spatiotemporal spectral asymmetric fusion network that explicitly models frontotemporal hemispheric asymmetry to decode emotions from low-channel EEG. STSANet achieved accuracies of 86.80% on the SEED dataset and 87.43% on a self-collected dataset, demonstrating robustness under cross-validation and highlighting the importance of spatial asymmetry modeling.

papers.title: Human P301L tau expression in mice alters neuronal excitability independent of neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: Using JNPL3(P301L) tau transgenic mice, this study investigated age-dependent electrophysiological changes from 3 to 10 months and found increased EEG power in higher frequency bands in hippocampus and cortex that was present early and stable over time, independent of progressive AT8 tau aggregates and neuroinflammation. The results suggest that P301L tau expression alters neuronal excitability independently of neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Sleep Variability From Routine Nursing Observation and Wearable Actigraphy for Early Risk Stratification in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients: Prospective Observational Study
papers.summary: Prospective observational study assessed whether early sleep instability during the first 7 days of hospitalization predicts prolonged length of stay in 94 acute psychiatric inpatients using wrist actigraphy and routine nursing observation. Greater actigraphy-derived sleep variability was associated with prolonged hospitalization (OR 2.42 per 1-hour increase; AUC 0.75), and nursing-derived sleep variability also carried independent prognostic information (adjusted OR 3.02; AUC 0.70).

papers.title: Gabapentin-Induced Severe Vivid Nightmares: A Case Series and Brief Review.
papers.summary: This case series reports two patients with spinal pain syndromes who developed severe vivid nightmares during gabapentin treatment, which resolved after discontinuation and transition to pregabalin. The report reviews literature on gabapentin's effects on sleep architecture and discusses potential mechanisms and management strategies.

papers.title: Acute caffeine supplementation as a nutrition-based strategy to mitigate sleep-loss-related cognitive and operational performance impairments in military personnel: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of seven randomized controlled trials evaluated acute caffeine supplementation as a countermeasure for sleep-loss-related performance impairments in military personnel. Caffeine significantly improved vigilance and response performance (SMD=0.73), complex cognitive performance (SMD=0.54), and military task performance (SMD=0.45) compared to placebo, with the most consistent benefits for vigilance and response speed.

papers.title: Management of residual excessive daytime sleepiness in depression: An AFPBN consensus using the nominal group technique.
papers.summary: A national expert consensus using the nominal group technique defined residual excessive daytime sleepiness in depression (rEDS-dep) as a multidimensional syndrome persisting >3 months despite adequate treatment, with agreed assessment (including HSI, actigraphy) and stepwise management prioritizing psychotropic reassessment, circadian interventions, and second-line wake-promoting agents. After two voting rounds, 48 of 70 statements were retained, with 35 reaching strong consensus.

papers.title: Observational Assessment of the Effect of Sleep Bruxism on Oxyhaemoglobin Saturation:A Preliminary Study.
papers.summary: In an observational polysomnographic study of 90 adults without obstructive sleep apnoea, individuals with sleep bruxism showed a significantly lower maximum oxyhaemoglobin saturation index compared with controls (p=0.04), while minimum and mean saturation did not differ. The difference was small and within normal physiological limits.

papers.title: Sleep disturbances as an early indicator of psychotic disorders in adolescents and young adults.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that sleep disturbances affect up to 70% of individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis and 80% of those with schizophrenia, involving overlapping dopaminergic, serotonergic, and hormonal pathways. It highlights screening tools (questionnaires, actigraphy, polysomnography) and sleep-focused interventions, particularly cognitive behavioral therapy, as promising for early detection and prevention.

papers.title: Component- and dimension-level network associations between sleep quality and health-related quality of life in older adults with hypertension.
papers.summary: In 2,257 older adults with hypertension, a component- and dimension-level network analysis of sleep quality and health-related quality of life identified usual activities as the highest centrality node, with sleep efficiency and subjective sleep quality showing the strongest bridge centrality. Network structure and global strength did not differ significantly by depressive-symptom status.

papers.title: A significant enrichment that is not: spatial nulls, co-expression, and the imaging transcriptomics of EEG alpha-power genetics
papers.summary: This imaging transcriptomics study tested whether EEG alpha-power genetics is spatially enriched in cortical alpha generators using MAGMA and Allen Human Brain Atlas data. Although a standard spin test suggested enrichment, the signal was not band-specific, did not replicate across alpha phenotypes, and was unremarkable against co-expression-matched gene-set nulls, indicating no regionally specific transcriptomic signature and highlighting the need for gene-set nulls alongside spatial nulls.

papers.title: Whose rhythms? Rhythmic agency, rhythmic justice, and circadian health in the menopausal transition.
papers.summary: This commentary introduces rhythmic agency (capacity to shape circadian-regulating conditions) and rhythmic justice (uneven distribution of that capacity) to reframe circadian disruption during the menopausal transition as a problem of social organization rather than individual behaviour. It outlines research directions and policy levers such as work scheduling, nighttime communication norms, urban lighting, and caregiving support.

papers.title: Roles in brain stimulation, recording and interpreting neuroimaging data: a systematic survey of 26 countries on current practices in EEG, MRI, TCD, TMS and FUS.
papers.summary: A systematic survey of 26 countries found that EEG and brain MRI are typically performed by technicians and interpreted by physicians, while transcranial Doppler, transcranial magnetic stimulation, and focused ultrasound stimulation are predominantly performed and interpreted by physicians. The authors report a significant absence of local guidelines for responsibilities in TMS and FUS and call for standardized national protocols.

papers.title: Frequency-specific dynamic characteristics of brain networks during salt taste perception: an EEG-based functional and effective connectivity analysis.
papers.summary: EEG data from 20 healthy participants during salt taste perception were analyzed using phase locking value, graph theory, and partial directed coherence. Salt stimulation enhanced whole-brain and inter-subnetwork phase synchronization, with the strongest response at low concentration, and low-intensity salty stimulation enhanced beta-band effective connectivity from the gustatory perception subnetwork to the multisensory integration subnetwork.

papers.title: Sleep Quality and Depressive Symptoms Among Pregnant Women in the Third Trimester: A Cross-Sectional Latent Profile and Network Analysis.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 471 third-trimester pregnant women identified four sleep-quality profiles, with the moderate multidimensional sleep impairment group showing significantly higher global network strength of sleep quality-depressive symptom associations than the good sleep quality group. PSQI6 (daytime dysfunction) had the highest bridge strength across all analyzed networks.

papers.title: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy pre-ictal oscillations recorded simultaneously with stereo-EEG.
papers.summary: Simultaneous stereo-EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy recordings from five patients showed ultra-slow hemodynamic oscillations (0.002-0.004 Hz) preceding SEEG-defined seizure onset in three patients and 10 of 16 seizures. These pre-ictal oscillations were unlikely to occur by chance and often formed spatial clusters corresponding to seizure onset hypotheses.

papers.title: Sleep duration and oral functional impairment: potential involvement of monocyte-related inflammation.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 8,252 adults, non-optimal sleep duration was associated with perceived masticatory difficulties, with a significant indirect effect mediated by monocyte count. Monocyte-related inflammation was identified as the sole significant mediator, suggesting a potential inflammatory pathway linking sleep and oral function.

papers.title: HbA1c reconsidered: glycated haemoglobin in the era of dynamic erythrocyte glucose metabolism.
papers.summary: Proposes that HbA1c reflects erythrocyte intracellular glucose exposure rather than solely mean plasma glucose, based on evidence that chronic hypoxia upregulates GLUT1 and alters glucose uptake. Reviews reported HbA1c discordance in conditions such as high-altitude populations, sleep apnoea, and critical illness, and offers a testable research framework without changing clinical practice.

papers.title: Narcolepsy-like presentations in intellectual disability with comorbid epilepsy and obstructive sleep apnea: a case-based diagnostic analysis and literature-informed discussion.
papers.summary: Presents a case-based diagnostic analysis of a 34-year-old woman with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and obstructive sleep apnea who presented with excessive daytime sleepiness and nocturnal events. After diagnosis and treatment with levetiracetam and CPAP, nocturnal episodes resolved and Epworth Sleepiness Scale improved from 18/24 to 6/24.

papers.title: Intensive care unit nurses' perceptions of night-work-related chronic fatigue and cognitive function: a cross-sectional survey.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 50 ICU nurses found strong perceptions that night work causes chronic fatigue and impairs attention, short-term memory, and working memory. No subgroup differences survived FDR correction, and the study was powered only to detect large effects.

papers.title: Post-Stroke Recrudescence During the Perioperative Period: Potential Roles of Anesthetic and Sedative Agents.
papers.summary: Narrative review of post-stroke recrudescence (PSR) during the perioperative period, examining anesthetic and sedative agents as potential triggers. Evidence is strongest for benzodiazepines like midazolam, while evidence for other agents is limited; PSR is a diagnosis of exclusion and further prospective studies are needed.

papers.title: The association between anxiety symptoms and sleep quality in people living with HIV/AIDS: the mediating effect of social support, psychological resilience and coping strategies.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 241 people living with HIV/AIDS examining the relationship between anxiety symptoms and sleep quality and the mediating roles of social support, psychological resilience, and positive coping style. Social support (7.2%), positive coping (9.6%), and resilience (13.3%) partially mediated the association between anxiety and sleep quality.

papers.title: Preoperative and postoperative ultrasound guided intercostal nerve blockade on postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing video assisted thoracic surgery (VATS): a prospective randomized comparative study.
papers.summary: Randomized trial comparing preoperative versus postoperative ultrasound-guided intercostal nerve block in 172 VATS patients. Postoperative block reduced moderate-to-severe resting pain in first 24h (11.9% vs 28.4%), lowered opioid consumption at 24 and 48h, and improved sleep quality during first two postoperative nights.

papers.title: Lifestyle Management for Pregnant Women with Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome Based on Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine: A Group Consensus.
keywords: integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine
papers.summary: Developed a group consensus on lifestyle management for pregnant women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) using a modified Delphi process with 25 multidisciplinary experts. After two rounds, consensus was reached on 5 primary, 15 secondary, and 22 tertiary indicators across exercise, diet, psychological health, sleep, and environment, with improved consensus metrics and 100% response rate.

papers.title: Lifestyle Behaviors and their association with self-rated health among university students in Spain: A cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 453 university students in Spain evaluating associations between lifestyle behaviors and self-rated health (SRH). Perceived stress was strongly associated with unfavorable SRH (OR=1.10), while male gender (OR=0.46) and Mediterranean diet adherence (OR=0.82) were associated with lower odds of unfavorable SRH; physical activity, sleep quality, and substance use showed no independent associations.

papers.title: Depressive symptoms, insomnia, and burnout among health-care workers in an integrated medical alliance in Shanghai: implications for workforce well-being and health-system management.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional survey of 494 healthcare workers in a Shanghai medical alliance assessing depressive symptoms, anxiety, stress, insomnia, and burnout. High prevalences of mild-or-worse symptoms were found (47.6% depression, 48.6% anxiety, 29.4% stress, 51.4% above ISI threshold), with on-call work associated with higher depression, anxiety, and insomnia scores in exploratory adjusted models; most subgroup differences did not survive multiplicity correction.

papers.title: Circadian Syndrome and Stress Urinary Incontinence in Adult American Women: A NHANES Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2007-2018 data (5758 women) examining the association between circadian syndrome (CircS) and stress urinary incontinence (SUI). In the fully adjusted model, women with CircS had significantly higher odds of SUI (OR=1.250, 95% CI 1.033-1.513), with a significant interaction by age (P<0.001); no significant association was found for the number of CircS components.

papers.title: The Role and Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence in Pulmonary Function Tests: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review assessed the diagnostic accuracy of AI-based interpretation of pulmonary function tests across 47 studies, finding that AI consistently outperformed non-specialists and improved accuracy when used as an adjunct, with the strongest evidence for COPD diagnosis. The authors conclude that AI should serve as a supportive triage or screening tool rather than an independent diagnostic decision-maker.

papers.title: Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms Among Early-Year Medical Students in Pakistan: Prevalence, Associated Factors, and Mental Health Service Implications-A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: A multicenter cross-sectional survey of 1,630 early-year medical students in Pakistan found high prevalences of anxiety symptoms (46.4%) and depressive symptoms (57.8%). Peer pressure was strongly associated with greater symptom severity, while sleeping 7–8 hours per night was associated with lower odds of severe symptoms.

papers.title: National mortality trends due to OSA and respiratory failure in U.S adults from 1999-2023: Insights from the CDC-WONDER database.
papers.summary: Analysis of CDC WONDER data from 1999–2023 found that age-adjusted mortality rates for obstructive sleep apnea and respiratory failure in U.S. adults increased steeply from 0.25 to 2.26 per 100,000 (AAPC 9.3). Disparities were observed by sex, race, urbanization, and region, with the highest burden among non-Hispanic Black individuals, nonmetropolitan areas, and the Midwest.

papers.title: Feasibility of millet-based gluten free and casein free diet in children with autism spectrum disorders: A 12-week pilot study in India.
papers.summary: This 12-week single-arm pilot study in India evaluated a millet-based gluten-free, casein-free diet in children aged 4–6 with autism spectrum disorder, finding high acceptability and adherence (80%). Caregivers reported improvements in gastrointestinal comfort (70%), sleep quality (60%), and hyperactivity (55%), alongside increased cereal and pulse intake and reduced fat consumption.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of different modifications of the Caprini risk score in bariatric surgery.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 120 patients undergoing laparoscopic bariatric surgery, postoperative VTE occurred in 5.0%, and a modified Caprini risk score (CRS 2010) incorporating estimated fat apron weight ≥11 kg and severe obstructive sleep apnea showed improved predictive accuracy (AUC 0.866) with an optimal cut-off of ≥12 points.

papers.title: A Four-Year Diagnostic Journey to Acute Intermittent Porphyria in a 19-Year-Old Woman: Lessons on Recognizing Neurovisceral Clues.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 19-year-old woman with a four-year diagnostic delay for acute intermittent porphyria, initially misdiagnosed with pseudoseizures, whose fecal total porphyrins were elevated (72.3 nmol/g) while plasma and urinary porphyrins were normal. The authors highlight that normal urinary ALA and PBG outside an acute attack do not exclude AIP and that fecal porphyrin analysis can provide complementary diagnostic evidence.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
